candidate_sentence_map.S1: Nordecon’s financial performance weakened in 2025 compared with the previous year, although the group strengthened its order book and expects business volumes to increase in 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue declined by 7% to €208.3 million, primarily because Buildings segment revenue fell by approximately 10% to €168.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Infrastructure revenue increased by 10% to €39.9 million, supported by road construction, maintenance and Rail Baltica-related work.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Buildings still represented the majority of revenue, with an 81% share, while Infrastructure accounted for 19%.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Profitability deteriorated as gross profit decreased to €13.5 million from €16.8 million and gross margin fell to 6.5% from 7.5%.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Operating profit declined by 30% to €5.7 million, reducing the operating margin to 2.7% from 3.6%, below the group’s target of consistently exceeding 3%.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: EBITDA fell to €8.3 million from €11.0 million, and the EBITDA margin declined to 4.0% from 4.9%.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Lower administrative expenses, which decreased by 14% to €6.8 million due mainly to reduced performance-based pay, partly offset the pressure on operating results.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Net profit declined by 51% to €2.5 million, while profit attributable to Nordecon’s owners fell to €1.4 million from €3.8 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Earnings per share decreased to €0.05 from €0.12.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Results were significantly affected by higher net finance costs, which increased to €3.0 million from €2.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: The main factor was a €750 thousand foreign-exchange loss arising from the weakening of the Ukrainian hryvnia against the euro, compared with €258 thousand in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Credit losses also increased to €354 thousand from €20 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Operating cash flow remained positive at €1.2 million, compared with €1.1 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: However, investing activities used €2.8 million, including €2.9 million placed in long-term deposits to secure guarantee limits, while financing activities used €1.2 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Consequently, cash and cash equivalents declined to €5.3 million from €8.2 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Liquidity remained relatively constrained, with the current ratio at 0.93, broadly unchanged from 0.94 at the end of 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The principal positive development was the 30% increase in the order book to €273.1 million at year-end.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: New contracts secured during the year totalled €235.0 million, including major Rail Baltica, road, public-building, defence and commercial projects.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Infrastructure’s share of the order book rose to 42% from 18%, while Buildings’ share declined to 58% from 82%.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: About 69% of the backlog is scheduled for execution in 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: Estonia’s construction market stabilised during the year, with activity improving in the second half, although competition, rising material prices and public-investment levels remain important risks.

evaluation.label: Yes
evaluation.justification: All six key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K1 is covered through multiple sentences detailing revenue decline, margin contractions, profit reductions, EPS drop, and the foreign exchange loss driver. K2 is fully covered with segment revenue changes and revised revenue shares. K3 is represented by the order book growth, Infrastructure segment contribution, and 2026 execution schedule. K4 is captured through operating, investing, and financing cash flows. K5 is covered by cash and cash equivalents, current ratio, and short-term borrowings. K6 is addressed through stable employee count and reduced staff costs due to lower performance-based pay.
